review.finding: guardExistingTarget's lstat had no ENOENT tolerance, so a register file deleted between the caller's existsSync check and this lstat call (the register has a real second writer -- leadwright's own daemon) propagated as an unhandled exception into a bare 500 instead of a graceful 404.
review.suggestion: Fixed: guardExistingTarget now catches ENOENT and returns a new {ok:false, status:404, error:"vanished"} variant; performRelease's preGuard/postGuard map it to the same not-found ReleaseOutcome the existsSync check already produces. Regression test added (mocked lstat throwing ENOENT).

review.finding: A second, independent OrgSymlinkEscapeError class duplicated the one already exported from decisions-lock.ts and reused by countersign.ts/file-write.ts -- structurally identical but a different type, so an instanceof check against the wrong import would silently fail to match.
review.suggestion: Fixed: removed the local class, import and re-export OrgSymlinkEscapeError from decisions-lock.ts instead, matching countersign.ts's existing pattern.

review.finding: ALL_ENDPOINTS (the list proving every /api/external/org/* route shares the same host+secret gate) was not updated to include the three new endpoints; none of the new route test files exercise createOrgRouter, so nothing would catch a future regression where one of the three routes stops being covered by the shared middleware.
review.suggestion: Fixed: added GET last-run, GET beat-register, and POST beat-register/release to ALL_ENDPOINTS. All parametrized gate cases pass for the three new routes (38 tests total in routes.test.ts, up from 20).

review.finding: performRelease was ~82 lines, over the 50-line guideline (advisory, not blocking) -- reviewer noted no action required unless it grows further.
review.suggestion: It did grow further (to ~115 lines) picking up the vanished-guard and duplicate-fault fixes, so applied the reviewer's own suggested extraction: pre-lock existence/guard check moved to checkRegisterReachable(), post-release audit append moved to recordRecoveryAudit(), leaving only the lock-acquire/critical-section/release in performRelease's body.

external_cascade_findings.finding: existsSync-gated guard skipped entirely for a dangling audit.jsonl symlink (existsSync follows symlinks and reports a dangling one as absent); openSync(path,'a') would then create/write through it outside leadsRoot.
external_cascade_findings.suggestion: Fixed: replaced with ensureAuditFile (wx flag, O_CREAT|O_EXCL -- fails EEXIST against ANY pre-existing path including a dangling symlink, without following it) + an UNCONDITIONAL guardExistingTarget call after, mirroring decisions-lock.ts's own already-reviewed ensureFile pattern verbatim.

external_cascade_findings.finding: A duplicate-sessionId fault where the FIRST matching entry is closed and a SECOND is open made release silently no-op on the open entry forever (find() picked the first match), contradicting FR-01.70(D)'s 'never resolved by picking one' principle applied only to reads.
external_cascade_findings.suggestion: Fixed: release now checks for >1 match on the requested sessionId BEFORE any mutation and returns 409 {ok:false, reason:"fault"} without touching the register or writing an audit line -- extends the existing read-side fault principle to the write path without inventing new leadwright-side recovery semantics.

external_cascade_findings.finding: Register close and audit append are non-atomic (audit append happens after the lock is released); a crash between them leaves a recovered-but-unaudited entry with no retry path to add the missing audit line.
external_cascade_findings.suggestion: Disclosed, not fixed. This is the SAME limitation already identified and explicitly decided across two prior review rounds (Plan Review PR-9, Internal Plan Review) specifically to mirror leadwright's own recoverRegisterEntry ordering -- the task brief instructs mirroring that contract rather than inventing a divergent (un-mirrored) recovery mechanism leadwright itself doesn't have. Re-affirmed rather than re-litigated; see the iterate spec's Plan Review + Internal Plan Review sections and the MIRRORED LIMITATION comment on recordRecoveryAudit.
